nodes.summary: For every valid color code $c$ (a pair of bits other than $11$), the code of the color that $c$ decodes to is $c$.
nodes.title: Re-encoding a decoded valid color

nodes.summary: The code of a color $c \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ is the pair of bits whose first bit is $1$ iff $c = 2$ and whose second bit is $1$ iff $c = 1$: $0 \mapsto 00$, $1 \mapsto 01$ and $2 \mapsto 10$.
nodes.title: Two-bit code of a color

nodes.summary: For all bit strings $x$ and $w$, the verifier accepts $(x, w)$ iff there are a natural number $n$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers such that $x$ is the encoding of the graph with $n$ vertices and edge list $E$, both entries of every pair in $E$ are less than $n$, $w$ has at least $2n$ bits, the color code of every vertex $i < n$ in $w$ is valid, and for every $(u, v) \in E$ with $u \ne v$ the color codes…
nodes.title: Acceptance condition of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: The verifier accepts an input $x$ and a witness $w$ (bit strings) iff $x$ decodes to a number $n$ and an edge list $E$, every endpoint of an edge in $E$ is less than $n$, $w$ has at least $2n$ bits, every vertex $i < n$ has a valid color code in $w$ (bits $2i$ and $2i + 1$, not $11$), and the two ends of every edge $(u, v) \in E$ with $u \ne v$ have different color codes.
nodes.title: The 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: For every $n$, every map $f$ from $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ to pairs of bits and every $i < n$, the color code of vertex $i$ in the flattening of the list $f(0), \dots, f(n - 1)$ is $f(i)$.
nodes.title: Color codes of a flattened coloring

nodes.summary: For every list $cs$ of pairs of bits and every natural number $i$, the color code of vertex $i$ in the flattening of $cs$ is the $i$-th pair of $cs$ (counting from $0$) if $i$ is less than the length of $cs$, and $00$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Color codes of flattened pairs

nodes.summary: The color code of vertex $i$ in a bit string $w$ is the pair of bits at positions $2i$ and $2i + 1$ of $w$ (counting from $0$), where a position past the end of $w$ reads as $0$. The codes $00$, $01$, $10$ stand for the colors $0$, $1$, $2$; $11$ is invalid.
nodes.title: Color code of a vertex in a witness

nodes.summary: A bit string $x$ is in 3-COLOR iff some bit string $w$ of length at most $2|x|$ is accepted together with $x$ by the 3-COLOR verifier.
nodes.title: 3-COLOR is verified by the witness check

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $es$ be a list of pairs of natural numbers whose entries are all less than $n$. The graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with edge list $es$ (symmetrized, loops dropped) is 3-colorable iff there is a list $w$ of exactly $2n$ bits such that, writing the color code of vertex $i$ for the pair of bits $2i$ and $2i+1$ of $w$, the color code of every vertex $i < n$ is valid (not $11$), and…
nodes.title: 3-colorability by witness bits

nodes.summary: For a bit list $w$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the color codes of the vertices $0, 1, \dots, n-1$ in $w$, in that order, where the color code of vertex $i$ is the pair of bits $2i$ and $2i+1$ of $w$ (a missing bit reads as false).
nodes.title: Witness colors of the first $n$ vertices

nodes.summary: For lists $cs$ and $ds$ of pairs of bits, the flattening of the concatenation of $cs$ and $ds$ is the concatenation of the flattening of $cs$ and the flattening of $ds$.
nodes.title: Flattening a concatenation

nodes.summary: For a pair of bits $c = (a, b)$ and a list $cs$ of pairs of bits, the flattening of the list with head $c$ and tail $cs$ is the list with $a$ first, then $b$, then the flattening of $cs$.
nodes.title: Flattening a nonempty list

nodes.summary: The flattening of the empty list of pairs of bits is the empty list of bits.
nodes.title: Flattening the empty list

nodes.summary: The flattening of a list $[(a_1, b_1), \dots, (a_k, b_k)]$ of pairs of bits is the list of bits $[a_1, b_1, \dots, a_k, b_k]$.
nodes.title: Flattening pairs of bits

nodes.summary: For every list $cs$ of pairs of bits, the flattening of $cs$ has length $2|cs|$, two bits per pair.
nodes.title: Length of a flattening

nodes.summary: For each color $c \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, the code of $c$ (which is $00$, $01$ or $10$) is a valid color code, that is, it is not $11$.
nodes.title: Color codes are valid

nodes.summary: A color code, a pair of bits $(c_1, c_2)$, is valid when it is not $11$, that is, when $c_1$ and $c_2$ are not both $1$.
nodes.title: Valid color code

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with token list $t(\varphi)$, let $o$ be a bit list and $v$ a Boolean. Started at its start label with local state $v$, with the token stack holding $t(\varphi)$ reversed, the output stack holding $o$ and every other stack empty, the emitter machine reaches the label $\mathsf{done}$ within $500\,(|t(\varphi)| + 1)^4$ steps, in some local state and with some stacks whose output stack…
nodes.title: Correctness and step bound of the 3-COLOR emitter

nodes.summary: For every color $c \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, decoding the two-bit code of $c$ (where $0 \mapsto 00$, $1 \mapsto 01$, $2 \mapsto 10$) gives back $c$.
nodes.title: Decoding a color code recovers the color

nodes.summary: The color in $\{0, 1, 2\}$ of a pair of bits $(a, b)$, writing $0$ for false and $1$ for true: $(0, 1)$ decodes to $1$, $(1, 0)$ decodes to $2$, and both $(0, 0)$ and the invalid code $(1, 1)$ decode to $0$.
nodes.title: Decoding a color code

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
